title: Ideal tensor sections are the kernel of closed restriction
statement: Let $j:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $I=j.ker$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], let $M$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $m\in\mathbb N$. Write $N=M^{\otimes m}$, and let $r_Z$ be restriction of global sections given by the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback] [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. The ideal multiplication map $\mu:I\otimes N\to N$ is injective on global sections, and $r_Z(t)=0$ if and only if $t=\mu(s)$ for some global section $s$ of $I\otimes N$.

source.place: Modules Lemma 08KS and Varieties Lemma 09NX, extension by zero

proof.text: Tensoring the ideal inclusion by the invertible tensor power preserves monomorphisms. Thus its multiplication map is mono and its categorical image is isomorphic to its source.

The quotient theorem [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] makes the image inclusion a kernel fork for the chosen pullback unit. Use uniqueness of limits to identify this kernel with the categorical kernel, and compose with the image-source isomorphism. Comparing adjunctions changes the unit by an isomorphism of its target, so does not change which sections it kills.

Evaluation on the top open preserves kernels. Transport its concrete range description along the kernel-source isomorphism. This gives both injectivity of the multiplication map and equivalence between zero restriction and being in its range.
